Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Core Vision

The Green Party presents itself as the only party offering genuine hope amid Britain's cost-of-living crisis, climate emergency, and crumbling public services. Despite being one of the world's richest nations, the UK sees nurses using food banks, schools deteriorating, and healthcare becoming inaccessible. The manifesto argues that climate solutions and social justice are inseparable—addressing one addresses the other.

## Health and Social Care

The NHS faces its worst crisis in 80 years due to deliberate Conservative underfunding. Greens would invest £28bn annually by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, ensuring universal NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), boosting staff pay, and fiercely opposing privatisation. Mental health would achieve parity with physical health, with therapy access within 28 days.

Social care would receive £20bn annually, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, with improved pay and career structures for carers.

## Housing

With over a million households on council waiting lists and homes costing 8.3 times average earnings, Greens would build 150,000 social homes annually, end right-to-buy, empower councils to introduce rent controls, and end no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes to high energy-efficiency standards, reducing bills and emissions simultaneously.

## Energy and Climate

The manifesto demands urgent climate action, criticising the 2050 net-zero target as insufficiently ambitious. Greens would end new fossil fuel extraction, cancel licences like Rosebank, eliminate oil and gas subsidies, and introduce a carbon tax starting at £120/tonne. Wind would provide 70% of electricity by 2030, with community ownership of energy infrastructure. Nuclear power would be phased out as expensive and dangerous. A just transition would protect workers in carbon-intensive industries through retraining and community investment.

## Economy and Work

Greens propose £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. They would introduce a £15/hour minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repeal anti-union legislation, and move toward a four-day working week. Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and disability benefits would rise 5%.

## Public Finances

Wealth would be taxed fairly: a 1-2% annual wealth tax on assets above £10m, capital gains aligned with income tax rates, and reformed inheritance tax. A carbon tax would raise up to £80bn by parliament's end. These measures would raise £50-70bn annually, falling on those most able to pay.

## Nature and Environment

Britain is among the world's most nature-depleted countries. Greens would pass a Rights of Nature Act giving nature legal personhood, protect 30% of land and seas by 2030, ban harmful pesticides, and bring water companies into public ownership to end sewage pollution. A new Right to Roam would reconnect people with nature.

## Education and Transport

Education would see £8bn investment in schools, £5bn for SEND provision, restored maintenance grants, and scrapped tuition fees. Transport investment would reach £10bn annually for rail and buses, with free bus travel for under-18s, railways renationalised, and £2.5bn yearly for cycling and walking infrastructure. Domestic flights under three hours by train would be banned.

## Democracy and Rights

Greens would replace first-past-the-post with proportional representation, give 16-year-olds the vote, replace the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and defend the Human Rights Act. They support Scottish and Welsh self-determination and would scrap legislation restricting protest rights.

## International

The manifesto calls for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, and ending UK arms exports to Israel. Overseas aid would rise to 1% of GNI, with additional climate finance. Greens support rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and cancelling Trident.

The manifesto concludes that voting Green represents choosing "real hope and real change" for a secure future on a safe planet.
